intro.title: Tolerance
paragraphs: Your dream is to become a successful entrepreneur and create a business that brings people together.

You have just been hired by a large multinational company, where people from different cultures, backgrounds, and professions work together. Working at this company is a learning experience for you, as by completing various challenges within it, you will acquire skills included in the POMEIL Competency Map, which are essential for every entrepreneur.

Today you enter a tranquil co-working office arranged for discussion and reflection. Amelia and Marco are here preparing for Open Culture Day, but they have a disagreement about how to organize the event. They could use your help.

dialogues.greet:
Hi, it's nice to see you here. I'm really glad you joined us — we could use some fresh ideas today. My colleague Marco and I had a disagreement about how to organize a large event for our company. It's our Open Culture Day, where we try to promote tolerance, identify challenges, and strengthen equality in our multicultural workplace.

But our perspectives on how to plan it are very different, and we may need your help to find a way forward.

dialogues.puzzle1Done: Was it hard? Or was it easy? But in the end, you did it, so we're ready to move on from this key point. I have to admit that your tolerance is growing with each completed task, so we have some more for you.

dialogues.frameFound: Those reflections will help you to build up your tolerance strong and solid. So, now we have pretty much a lot, and we're ready to check. Can we move on with our tolerance? So, get ready for the next quizzes!
dialogues.finalWords:
I got your feelings. Probably it was not easy. But life is not always easy. Now you had few scenarios that worked out. It was a great practice to consider some work and life-related situations to develop your tolerance. And I can tell, you did great. I'm proud of you!

So never give up and keep on going!
dialogues.skillComplete: You achieved the ability of tolerance. Now it's fully developed. You may go back and try the quizzes out anytime when you feel like you need it.
dialogues.completion:
You have completed the final skill in the list!
You can now explore any skills you haven't tried yet, or return to the ones you want to practice again. The map will help guide you wherever you choose to go next.

Feel free to share this game and its link with friends, colleagues, or anyone who may need support adjusting to a new country. This tool was created to empower entrepreneurs as they learn and grow.

You did a great job. Good luck, and thank you for being part of this journey.

dialogues.toleranceExplained: Tolerance in life means accepting that people have different beliefs, habits, and ways of seeing the world. It's about staying patient, open, and respectful even when someone thinks differently than you do.
dialogues.toleranceDetails:
Tolerance It's not a habit, It takes time, education and practice to achieve, here are some most common ways and situations where our tolerance ability can be improved:

1. Tolerance in Life — To develop tolerance in daily life, start by noticing your reactions when someone behaves or thinks differently than you. Practice pausing before judging, and choose curiosity instead of criticism. Listen to people's stories and try to understand what shaped their views.

2. Tolerance in Your Work Surroundings — To build tolerance at work, focus on open communication and calm, respectful listening. People come from different cultures and have different working styles, so ask for clarification instead of assuming and give teammates the space to express their ideas.

3. Tolerance in Your Household or Family — Tolerance at home begins with understanding that each family member has their own emotions, habits, and ways of thinking. Practice speaking kindly during disagreements and take time to explain your feelings without blaming. Set shared rules for communication — such as listening fully before responding.
dialogues.toleranceSummary: Tolerance grows when we learn to understand and respect differences in every part of our lives — at home, at work, and in the world around us. It develops through calm listening, open communication, and a willingness to adjust our perspective when needed. When we practice tolerance consistently, our relationships become stronger, conflicts become easier to solve, and our environments become safer and more supportive for everyone.

matching.title: Match the tolerance response to the situation
matching.instructions: Select a situation from Column A, then match it to the correct tolerance response in Column B.

items.1: Someone has a different opinion from you
items.2: A co-worker works slower than you expected
items.3: A family member gets upset during a conversation
items.4: You do not understand someone's words or accent

items.A: Listen calmly and let them finish speaking
items.B: Be patient and give them more time
items.C: Ask kindly for them to repeat or explain
items.D: Stay calm and try to understand their feelings

feedback.wrong: Think about which action shows patience and understanding. Tolerance means staying calm, listening well, and trying to understand the other person.
feedback.allCorrect: Excellent! You matched all tolerance responses correctly!

matching.answerOverlay:
The correct matches are:
1. Someone has a different opinion → Listen calmly and let them finish speaking
2. A co-worker works slower → Be patient and give them more time
3. A family member gets upset → Stay calm and try to understand their feelings
4. You do not understand someone's words → Ask kindly for them to repeat or explain

pattern.title: Teamwork pattern reading
pattern.instructions: Read each short story. Then choose the teamwork pattern that best matches what is happening. Look for teamwork behaviors, not negative reactions.

scenarios.text: A team is confused about a task. One person speaks calmly, asks everyone what they think, and writes down a plan they all agree on.
scenarios.hint: Good teamwork begins with calm talk and a plan the group creates together.

scenarios.text: A teammate is working slowly. Instead of complaining, another teammate offers help and asks if they want to divide the task.
scenarios.hint: Teamwork grows when people support each other instead of judging.

scenarios.text: During a disagreement, two coworkers stop talking over each other. They listen, repeat what they heard, and look for one idea they both can accept.
scenarios.hint: Teamwork improves when people listen first and find something they can agree on.

popupContent: Pause — Take a moment before responding. A short pause helps prevent emotional reactions and keeps communication respectful.
Listen — Give full attention to what the other person is saying. Listening openly helps you understand their experience before forming your own response.
Reflect — Consider why the situation feels tense or uncomfortable. Reflection helps separate assumptions from actual facts.
Ask — Use calm, curious questions to understand the other person's viewpoint. Asking shows respect and reduces misunderstandings.
Acknowledge — Recognize the feelings, perspectives, or experiences of others, even if you don't agree. Acknowledgment builds trust and reduces defensiveness.
Adapt — Be willing to adjust your communication or expectations when working with people from different backgrounds. Adaptability helps bridge cultural or personal differences.
Resolve — Look for a fair solution that respects everyone involved. Resolution is not about winning — it's about creating understanding and moving forward together.
Tolerance grows when you stay calm and try to understand people who are different from you.
You do not need to agree with everyone — showing respect is already a big step toward peace.
Every time you listen without judging, you make it easier to work, live, and communicate with others.
Small moments of patience can turn conflicts into understanding and help build stronger relationships.
